newsitem.title: UK: No show penalties successful for Air Canada.
newsitem.headline: No show penalties successful for Air Canada.

text.p: The stand taken by Air Canada from March 1 to penalise weekend no-shows of air cargo has greatly reduced the number of shipments booked but not flown, said Des Vertannes, the carrier's general manager cargo for Europe, Africa and the Middle East.
Air Canada did not lose business as result of this Europe-wide initiative, he said in an interview.
Some clients had to pay penalties as a result of the scheme but Vertannes said weekend no shows had fallen to between one and two percent from 18-20 percent previously.
Midweek no-shows were still too high at 8-12 percent but were down from 18-20 percent.
There is some pressure from shippers and forwarders for airlines to give compensation when shipments are not flown as booked.
Vertannes said that this may come "in time and to some degree" but exact definition would be important by both sides to avoid overly strict and unfair conditions.

Air Canada's no-show penalties allow cancellations but require the agent or shipper to give notice or face paying 50 percent of what it would have cost to fly the shipment. -Douglas Learmond, Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
